final.answer: GV-11-2 is a solenoid valve (Type 165, servo-controlled 2/2-way diaphragm valve), so yes, it needs electrical power to operate its coil. The documentation lists available supply voltages of 24V DC, 110V AC and 230V AC (with 50/60 Hz for AC), so 24 V DC will work — you do not need 230 V AC. Coil sets are ordered separately per voltage and gasket material (e.g. 198 808 029 for EPDM/24V DC, 198 808 030 for EPDM/230V AC, 198 808 032 for FKM/24V DC, 198 808 033 for FKM/230V AC), so make sure the fitted coil matches your supply.

final.answer: The valve operated by loop FIC-6-2 is FV-6-2, a Fisher ET/EAT globe-style control valve with cage guiding and a balanced valve plug. Leak-through when shut can come from either sealing element, and the documentation distinguishes them: with PTFE seating, the shutoff mechanism is a backup ring or spring-loading that forces the valve plug seal ring against the cage, so a leak there points to the plug seal ring (UHMWPE R30003 seal ring, with metal disk seat, PTFE disk and disk retainer in the standard PTFE-seat construction). With metal seating (standard for Cavitrol III cages, optional metal-to-metal for other valves), shutoff depends on the seat ring (e.g., S31600/S41600 seat ring or liner), so a leak there points to the seat ring. To check, perform a seat leak test: the trim cartridge is factory seat-leak tested to CL V shutoff, and the shutoff class depends on the seating chosen (Class IV standard with metal seating, Class V optional with metal seating, Class V/Vi with PTFE seating, and TSO trim tested to no leakage at shipment). If the valve fails its rated shutoff class on test, inspect the seat ring gasket and seat ring for metal-seat constructions, or the PTFE disk, seal ring and backup/spring-loading for soft-seat constructions.
